title: scheduler-driven-prefetch-with-kernel-hints-and-kvcache-merge-paths
author: Liam O'Connor
description: Motivation: customer workloads show uneven tail latency when short user messages are followed by long generations. The prefill stage historically runs in large contiguous chunks and picks kernels based on static heuristics; decode waits for prefill completion which causes underutilized GPU cycles and KV-cache thrashing for bursty traffic. This change implements a scheduler-driven prefetch path that (1) emits kernel-selection hints earlier in the pipeline so the kernel allocator can prepare fast paths, (2) breaks large prefill batches into targeted micro-prefetch slices aligned with active decode windows, and (3) merges KV-cache updates from overlapping prefetch slices into a single commit to avoid repeated cache churn. Design summary: - Scheduler now tracks per-request decode readiness and issues prefetch slices with an accompanying kernel_hint tag (eg: "matmul-fast-path:v2", "qkv-fuse:low-latency"). - Kernel allocator listens for kernel_hint events and pre-loads preferred kernels / selects quantized execution where latency estimates favor it. - Prefetch micro-slices are sized by a new heuristic (slice_size = max(8, min(64, predicted_decode_window_tokens))) that trades a small increase in incremental latency for higher overlap between prefill and decode. - KV cache updates from concurrent slices for the same session are aggregated in-memory and flushed as a single merge transaction at slice boundary or on decode start to reduce eviction churn. - Continuous-batching layer gains a "prefetch_priority" flag that prefers tiny speculative batches for sessions with imminent decode readiness. Compatibility and safety: the feature is opt-in via runtime config flags (runtime.scheduler.prefetch.enabled, runtime.kernel.hints.enabled) and defaults to off for older deployments. We added guardrails that revert to previous behavior if kernel preload fails or if KV merge latency exceeds a tunable threshold. Testing: microbenchmarks on p4d and A100 show 12-18% median latency improvement for conversational workloads with mixed short/long replies and up to 25% reduction in token-cost due to fewer KV evictions. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag and telemetry that measures KV merge latency, kernel warmup hit-rate, and decode-scheduling overlap ratio. Related: follows on from ENG-3121 (continuous batching refactor) and is intended to be composed with future conservative-prefetch experiments.
commits: 3 commits: 1) scheduler: add prefetch slice + kernel_hint events (author patch) 2) kernel: add kernel_hint listener and preload path (author patch) 3) kvcache: introduce merge buffer with commit-on-boundary and metrics (author tests)
review_comments: Priya Desai: Interesting approach — can you clarify how the kernel_hint taxonomy is maintained across model variants? I worry about explosion of hint types leading to poor cache locality.

Author (Liam O'Connor): We keep a small canonical set of hint families (eg: matmul-fast-path, qkv-fuse, small-batch-quant) and map model-variant specific suggestions to these families during onboarding. The mapper lives in kernel_allocator::hint_mapper and is updated when a model is registered. Added details in docs/ops/prefetch-feature-flag.md.

Marcello Ruiz: The KV merge buffer looks good but we saw a regression in one of the stress tests where merge latency spiked under memory pressure. Can we add a backpressure path to bypass merging when memory budget is low?

Author (Liam O'Connor): Added a memory-based bypass threshold (runtime.kv.merge_memory_bypass_mb) and a metric (kvcache.merge_bypass_count) so we can monitor bypass frequency. If memory is low we flush slices immediately instead of merging.
Evelyn Park: Unit tests passing; can we add an e2e that simulates many short prefill bursts interleaved with long decodes?
Author (Liam O'Connor): Added tests/integration/prefetch_kv_merge_test.rs that emulates mixed-burst traffic and asserts on reduced kvcache eviction and stable decode latency.
release_notes: Introduce scheduler-driven prefetch slices with kernel-selection hints and KV-cache merge buffering to reduce decode tail latency and KV churn; opt-in via runtime flags; metrics added: kvcache.merge_latency_ms, kernel_hint.warmup_hit_rate, scheduler.overlap_ratio.
